claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits superior plastic strain and toughness to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Atomic size differences among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr produce severe lattice distortion in equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Severe lattice distortion generates a uniformly distributed internal stress field.
The lattice-distortion-associated stress field facilitates activation of multiple slip systems.
Atomic size mismatch reduces local energy barriers for dislocation nucleation.
Atomic size mismatch enhances dislocation mobility.
Activation of multiple slips and enhanced dislocation mobility produce more homogeneous plastic deformation.
Distributed deformation suppresses localized dislocation pile-ups and stress concentrations that lead to brittle failure.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has a homogeneous, phase-pure BCC solid-solution structure.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is free of brittle intergranular phases.
Brittle intergranular phases are typically present in pure tungsten.
Commercially used pure tungsten has a conventional grain structure.
Under identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a lower creep rate than pure tungsten.
Under identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit less strain localization than pure tungsten.
Grain-boundary variations or secondary phases can affect deformation behavior and ductility.
The proposed comparison applies specifically at 800–1000°C in vacuum for samples with verified homogeneous microstructures.
Matching sample geometry, grain size, temperature, vacuum, and strain rate is intended to isolate intrinsic deformation behavior.

contradictions.description: The mechanism asserts reduced dislocation-nucleation barriers and generally enhanced dislocation mobility, while the outcome predicts a lower creep rate. The hypothesis does not distinguish mobility supporting plastic glide from mobility controlling creep or provide a compensating mechanism that reconciles these statements.
